title: W as spatial construction
slide_intent: Show how a small geometric change alters perceived space because a line can imply depth without shaded volume.
strategic_value: A repeated unfolding W can give Whitney a spatial vocabulary related to the museum environment.
demonstration: A stack of black lines changes from almost straight at the top to deeper angular Ws below.
practical_value: Compare successive depths to see how the same line construction moves between flat and spatial readings.

content_islands.name: Line sequence
content_islands.spec: Stack the repeated four-segment forms vertically; increase their depth toward the bottom without adding fill or shading.

reference_purposes.Intent: The adjacent essay explicitly describes a flat line revealing a spatial dimension through viewpoint and distance.
reference_purposes.Expression: The progressively deeper zigzags demonstrate a spatial interpretation of the mark.
